title: Integrated urban land cover analysis using deep learning and post-classification correction
relevance: Retrieves CANOPY-COVERED IMPERVIOUS SURFACES with a vector-oriented post-classification step, which is the exact inverse of our newly measured dominant failure mode: our model's recall roughly halves on canopy over impervious (0.32 vs 0.69 in 2016, a gap of 0.37-0.43 in every year tested). It lets us treat overhang as a named, addressable class with an existing method rather than as diffuse error, and its post-classification framing is a cheaper candidate than retraining. It also implies C-CAP's impervious-under-canopy layer is a deliberate product of this same logic, which is why C-CAP finds the pixels we miss.

title: Very High Resolution Images and Superpixel-Enhanced Deep Neural Forest Promote Urban Tree Canopy Detection
relevance: Reports that U-Net specifically is degraded by canopy shadow, producing high omission and low recall - which is our architecture and our symptom, and it supplies a mechanism for the over-impervious deficit that is distinct from the dark-foliage-on-dark-roof story we assumed. This lets us separate two candidate causes of the same gap: shadow cast ONTO the impervious surface versus low contrast between crown and roof, which are testable apart because shadow is sun-angle dependent and varies with acquisition time while roof contrast does not. If shadow dominates, the fix is radiometric or acquisition-aware, not structural, and the CHM channel would not help.

title: An Open and Transferable Deep Learning Framework for Mapping Urban Tree Canopy Using NAIP Imagery
relevance: A transferable canopy-mapping framework built on NAIP, which is the exact source of our 2019n and 2022n acquisitions, so it is the closest published analogue to the transfer problem our cross-sensor years pose. It gives us an external benchmark for what NAIP-based canopy recall should look like, which we currently have no way to calibrate against, and its open weights would let us test our imagery against a model that never saw Edmonds - a genuine held-out check that our own cross-year evaluation cannot provide. Published 2026, so it postdates every method in our pipeline.
